common.purpose: Resolve three I44 retirement design points for the Can tree: what removed launcher commands do, how the absence of legacy paths is proven, and what becomes of the tscheck committed-golden gate.

residual_proof.background: Once deletion lands, I44 owes a demonstration that predecessor paths are extinct, via static source-tree gating, behavior probing and dispatch searches, or both combined.
facts: Reachability from the surviving dispatch roots across package main leaves all predecessor parser, checker, evaluator, prover, and Z3-invocation symbols unreached, handing a static gate an exact property to enforce.
The current parse path already rejects predecessor syntax explicitly in fixtures, and tree searches can verify the launcher holds no Z3, extern-grant, or legacy-syntax dispatch.
Static gates risk decaying into allowlists and behavior probes risk overlooking present-but-unreachable code, giving each approach a blind spot covered by the other.

retired_command_ux.background: Four launcher commands vanish though their names linger in scripts, notes, and habit, so every stale invocation should fail loudly instead of quietly succeeding.
facts: Silent erasure sends explain, lint, baseline, and normalize into the generic usage error at exit 2, costing no code and treating those names as if they never existed.
Dedicated stubs exit 2 carrying a retired message per name, guiding stale callers while permanently lodging four dead names inside the launcher they left.
I41 already sets precedent with a retired-flag exit-2 error for the withdrawn lsp --baseline flag, proving explicit retirement errors exist in this codebase.

tscheck_fate.background: tscheck plus the tsc.yml workflow strictly typecheck committed .ts goldens beneath std and sketches, all of which this task deletes.
facts: Today the gate fails on predecessor rot through missing modules and tag-type mismatches, hence deletion clears failing subjects instead of breaking a passing signal.
Once includes match nothing, tsc reports no inputs and fails, so the present configuration cannot pass untouched after retirement.
I45 item 2 regrounds TypeScript gating in freshly emitted CI output, either adapting tscheck files that survive or recreating them following deletion.
